newsitem.title: CANADA: Noranda says contract talks progressing.
newsitem.headline: Noranda says contract talks progressing.

text.p: Noranda Inc said on Friday that it is making progress in contract talks with unionized workers at three of its divisions in New Brunswick.
"We're making good progress on language issues," Noranda president Courtney Pratt said in a telephone interview.
He said the company expects to begin discussing monetary and pension issues in the week of March 10.
"You could call the progress so far normal. We don't have any particular concerns over a strike," said Pratt.

The company is holding talks with the union representing 256 workers at the Heath Steele zinc and lead operation which produced 50,813 tonnes of zinc and 6,016 tonnes of lead in 1996. The last contract with the members of the United Steelworkers of America union expired on December 31, 1996.
The company is also negotiating with 992 United Steelworkers' members at its Brunswick mining division which produced 252,834 tonnes of zinc in 1996.
And talks are ongoing with 510 United Steelworkers' members at the Brunswick smelter which produced 71,750 tonnes of lead in 1996.
The contracts at the Brunswick smelter and the Brunswick mine ended on Friday. The company is negotiating separate contracts with all three divisions.
